name: L298N dual H-bridge motor driver
description: ST L298 dual full-bridge driver: runs two DC motors (or one bipolar stepper) forwards, backwards, braked or coasting, up to 2 A per bridge, from TTL/3.3 V logic inputs. Motor supply 5-35 V on the module, logic 5 V. Sold as: L298N dual H-bridge motor driver module (red 43 x 43 mm board with heatsink and 78M05 regulator, e.g. Handson Technology MDU-1049; terminals OUT1 OUT2 | +12V GND +5V | header ENA IN1 IN2 IN3 IN4 ENB | OUT3 OUT4).
eli5: Lets your board make two motors spin forwards or backwards, using a bigger battery than the board itself can supply.

pins.name: OUT1
pins.description: Motor A output 1 (screw terminal); connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: +12V
pins.description: Motor supply VS, 5-35 V on this module (chip allows up to 46 V). Keep the 5V-EN jumper only when this is 7-12 V

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground: common to the motor supply and the microcontroller

pins.name: +5V
pins.description: Logic supply VSS (4.5-7 V). Output of the on-board 78M05 when the 5V-EN jumper is fitted; otherwise feed 5 V in here

pins.name: ENA
pins.description: Enable bridge A (high = on, PWM for speed). Jumpered to 5 V on delivery = always full speed

pins.name: IN1
pins.description: Bridge A input 1 (TTL: high >= 2.3 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs work)

pins.name: ENB
pins.description: Enable bridge B (high = on, PWM for speed). Jumpered to 5 V on delivery

supplierQuery: L298N dual H-bridge motor driver module
buildNotes: Truth table (ST datasheet): EN high + IN1 high/IN2 low = forward, IN1 low/IN2 high = reverse, IN1 = IN2 = fast brake; EN low = motor coasts.
Connect the module GND to the microcontroller GND, or the IN signals have no reference.

5V-EN jumper fitted: the on-board 78M05 makes 5 V from +12V and the +5V terminal is an output - only for a motor supply of about 7-12 V. Remove the jumper above 12 V, or when the motor supply is under 7 V, and feed 5 V into +5V.
Never connect the +5V terminal to your board's 3V3 pin or feed it more than 7 V.
ENA/ENB are jumpered to 5 V (full speed). Pull the jumper and wire EN to a PWM pin for speed control; keep PWM under 25 kHz.
The bridge drops about 2-3 V (1.8-3.2 V at 1 A), so a 6 V motor needs roughly an 8-9 V supply. Small motors only from a USB 5 V pin; use a separate battery for anything bigger.
Each bridge is limited to 2 A continuous; the heatsink gets hot near that.

driver.code:
# L298N dual H-bridge motor driver (ST L298), MicroPython driver for ONE bridge (one DC motor).
# Make one L298N object per motor: bridge A = IN1, IN2, ENA; bridge B = IN3, IN4, ENB.
# Truth table from the ST L298 datasheet (Fig. 6, bidirectional DC motor control):
#   EN = H, C = H, D = L  -> forward
#   EN = H, C = L, D = H  -> reverse
#   EN = H, C = D         -> fast motor stop (brake)
#   EN = L, C/D = X       -> free-running motor stop (coast)
# Inputs are TTL: low <= 1.5 V, high >= 2.3 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive them directly.
# Speed: PWM the EN pin (remove the ENA/ENB jumper). The L298 commutation frequency is 25 kHz typ.,
# 40 kHz max, so the default 1 kHz is well inside the limit.
from machine import Pin, PWM


class L298N:
    def __init__(self, in_a, in_b, en=None, freq=1000):
        """in_a, in_b: GPIO numbers of the bridge's IN pins (IN1/IN2 or IN3/IN4).
        en: GPIO number of ENA/ENB, or None when the module's enable jumper is fitted (always full speed)."""
        self.a = Pin(in_a, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.b = Pin(in_b, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.pwm = None
        if en is not None:
            self.pwm = PWM(Pin(en), freq=freq, duty_u16=0)

    def _enable(self, speed):
        if self.pwm is not None:
            speed = max(0, min(100, speed))
            self.pwm.duty_u16(speed * 65535 // 100)

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        """Spin one way (IN_a high, IN_b low). speed 0-100 % needs the EN pin."""
        self.a.value(1)
        self.b.value(0)
        self._enable(speed)

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        """Spin the other way (IN_a low, IN_b high)."""
        self.a.value(0)
        self.b.value(1)
        self._enable(speed)

    def brake(self):
        """Fast motor stop: both inputs equal with the bridge enabled."""
        self.a.value(0)
        self.b.value(0)
        self._enable(100)

    def coast(self):
        """Free-running stop: EN low. Without an EN pin (jumper fitted) this falls back to brake()."""
        self.a.value(0)
        self.b.value(0)
        if self.pwm is not None:
            self.pwm.duty_u16(0)

    def stop(self):
        self.brake()

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from l298n import L298N

# Motor A on IN1/IN2; ENA jumper fitted, so it runs at full speed.
motor = L298N({IN1}, {IN2})
while True:
    motor.forward()
    print('motor A forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.brake()
    print('motor A stopped')
    time.sleep(1)
